rambla: Plaça Catalunya, La Rambla and La Boqueria
From the square, walk down La Rambla to the Mercat de la Boqueria, the city's most famous covered market: fruit stalls, jamón and juices.
gotic: The Cathedral, Carrer del Bisbe with its neo-Gothic bridge, Plaça Sant Jaume and Plaça Reial with the lampposts designed by the young Gaudí. The narrow lanes are the real reason to come.
born: El Born and Santa Maria del Mar
Santa Maria del Mar, the neighbourhood's great Gothic church, Carrer de Montcada with its medieval palaces and the Mercat del Born, the former covered market with the excavations of the 1714 city.
barceloneta: The old fishermen's quarter, with narrow streets and washing hung out to dry, then the seafront and the beach.
sagrada: Gaudí's basilica: the Nativity Façade, a walk around it and the full shot from Plaça de Gaudí, across the pond.
passeig: Passeig de Gràcia: Casa Batlló and La Pedrera
The avenue of Modernisme: the "bone" façade of Casa Batlló, the neighbouring houses of the Block of Discord and, five blocks up, La Pedrera. Look out for the ceramic bench-lampposts too.
sagradains: Inside the basilica: the forest of columns and the light through the stained glass, cool on the east side and warm on the west in the afternoon. Then the Passion Façade and the museum under the church.
parkguell: Gaudí's Monumental Zone: the stairway with the mosaic salamander, the Hypostyle Room and the long wavy bench with views over the whole city.
gracia: The former village swallowed by the city: Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila with its clock tower, Carrer de Verdi and, from outside, Casa Vicens, Gaudí's first house.
bunkers: The old anti-aircraft emplacements on top of Turó de la Rovira: a 360° panorama over all of Barcelona, from the Sagrada Família to the sea.
picasso: The museum in the Gothic palaces of Carrer de Montcada: Picasso's early years in Barcelona and the Meninas series.
batllo: Inside Gaudí's house: the main room overlooking Passeig de Gràcia, the courtyard of blue tiles and the terrace with its dragon-back roof.
santpau: Domènech i Montaner's former Modernista hospital, a 15-minute walk from the Sagrada Família along Avinguda de Gaudí: brick and ceramic pavilions, domes and gardens.
pedrera: Gaudí's last private house: the rooftop with its warrior-shaped chimneys, the arched attic and a period apartment.
mnac: Plaça d'Espanya, Magic Fountain and MNAC

From Plaça d'Espanya you climb between the Venetian towers to the Magic Fountain and the Palau Nacional, home of the museum of Catalan art: the terrace in front of the entrance has one of the best views of the city.
castell: The fortress on top of the hill, with terraces over the port and the sea. Go up by cable car, by bus or on foot through the gardens.
